documents.title: Policy 100-022: Howard University Artificial Intelligence (AI) Policy
documents.summary: Howard Policy 100-022 is a university-wide framework covering teaching, research, partnerships and work use. It sets no course-level AI rule: faculty set permissible use in syllabi and students ask when guidance is absent. Most of its content is data, IP and governance requirements.
documents.stance_why: The policy states that "Faculty shall establish and communicate, through course syllabi ... course requirements regarding the permissible and impermissible use of AI tools" and that students shall "seek clarification from the instructor" without course guidance, so it hands the decision to instructors.

units.why: This sets the institution-wide purpose: the policy exists "to ensure the responsible use of artificial intelligence" across academic, research and operational work. It is a framework preamble, so P56, actor all, informs.
units.anchor: to ensure the responsible use of artificial intelligence (AI)
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B admin. The sentence states the purpose of a policy that 'applies to all members of the Howard University community', so it addresses everyone, not only administrators. Final actor: all.

units.why: The policy "will be reviewed annually and updated as necessary", a review cycle held by the Responsible Officer; P54 fits, with admin as the actor.
units.anchor: This policy will be reviewed annually and updated as necessary

units.why: The rationale says AI "can enhance teaching and learning" when "used responsibly", a framing of AI as beneficial with conditions; P56 (framework principle) fits better than P44 because it is not about professional skill. [Final codes follow the reconciliation: see resolution_why.]
units.anchor: can enhance teaching and learning, support research and scholarship
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all and unit_stance permit; B coded admin and neutral. The sentence is a rationale ('can enhance teaching and learning ... AI also presents risks'); it takes no position on whether anyone may use AI, so unit_stance is neutral, and the preamble speaks to the whole community. Final: actor all, unit_stance neutral.

units.why: The rationale names risks "related to bias, accuracy, accessibility, privacy, data security, intellectual property"; this names harms (P53) and also touches privacy and IP, but P53 is the best single home because it lists bias and risks generally.
units.anchor: AI also presents risks related to bias, accuracy, accessibility, privacy, data security

units.why: The rationale states the policy "establishes a University-wide framework for the responsible use of AI" that "upholds academic integrity"; a scope and principles statement, P56.
units.anchor: establishes a University-wide framework for the responsible use of AI
units.resolution_why: A coded actor all, B admin. The framework 'establishes a University-wide framework' for everyone covered by the policy; it is addressed to the community, so actor all.

units.why: The scope clause says the policy "applies to all members of the Howard University community, including faculty, staff, students"; scope definition, P61 (defines what the policy covers).

units.why: Defines AI as systems that "perform tasks normally requiring human intelligence"; a definition setting scope, P61.
units.anchor: computer-based systems or software that perform tasks normally requiring human intelligence

units.why: Defines generative AI as systems that "generate new content, including text, images, audio, video, code"; code is explicitly in scope, P61.

units.frag_end: in response to user inputs or prompts.

documents.title: Initial Howard University Guidelines for use of Generative AI Tools
documents.summary: Early Provost guidelines setting values: bias mitigation, privacy, AI literacy, verification and fairness in academic-integrity cases. They tell schools and faculty to write their own policies and describe AI as a possible adjunct, not a substitute for thinking.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines say schools, colleges and faculty "should develop their own policies" and "There will likely be no one size fits all approach", while calling AI "useful adjunctive tools"; no single rule is set, so they delegate.

units.why: The guidelines separate generative AI from "Artificial General Intelligence" and describe it as systems that "produce various forms of human expression"; a definition, P61.
units.anchor: Generative AI refers to computer systems that produce various forms of human expression

units.why: 'It is imperative then to organize and affirm values, guidelines, and assumptions about these tools' frames the page as an institutional framework, P56.
units.anchor: It is imperative then to organize and affirm values, guidelines, and assumptions about these tools
units.resolution_why: Found only by coder B. The sentence 'It is imperative then to organize and affirm values, guidelines, and assumptions about these tools' is a statement of purpose for the guidance, separate from the learning rationale in the same sentence. Kept as coded.

units.why: The Provost says it is "imperative" to affirm values because "writing and voice production remain important modes of critical, artistic, and sense-based learning"; a learning rationale, P41.
